reasoning: The mechanism is real. AtomicFileWrite.swift:27 calls replaceItemAt with default options, which keeps the destination's existing permissions, and that path is only taken when the destination file already exists (AtomicFileWrite.swift:26). The claimed damage does not hold up, though. (1) The write never loosens anything. A file that was 0644 before is 0644 after, and anything the app creates itself goes through moveItem (line 29) at 0600. So the exposure is whatever someone else caused beforehand, and the write adds no new disclosure. (2) config.toml is tightened back to 0600 on every load (ConfigLoader.swift:74-78), before save() at ConfigLoader.swift:110 ever runs. (3) Every app-owned secret file lives under the Application Support or Caches directory for ai-taskbar, and both are forced to 0700 (Paths.swift:19-22 and 34-37). Other local users cannot traverse into those directories, so a 0644 mode on a file inside them exposes nothing. (4) The only secret outside those directories is ~/.codex/auth.json. It is rewritten only through FileCredentialReader.writeBack (FileCredentialReader.swift:74), which runs only with the opt-in manage_oauth_refresh = true (off by default per CLAUDE.md), and the Codex CLI owns that file's mode. At most this is a hardening and test gap: a promise to tighten on write that is not kept. It is not a real exposure of sensitive data, let alone a HIGH one.
